simple.meaning: פִּטְדָה (piṭdâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a gem , probably the topaz.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּטְדָה (H6357) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 28:17, with occurrences in Exodus, Job, Ezekiel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּטְדָה (H6357) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּטְדָה (H6357) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּטְדָה (piṭdâh) / H6357 is traced through Exodus 28:17, Exodus 39:10, Job 28:19, Ezekiel 28:13 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6357. pitdah מִּטְדָה noun feminine ( masculine according to Albr ZAW xvi (1896), 108 ) topaz or chrysolite (according to ᵐ5 τοπάζιον , ᵑ9 topazius , etc.; probably foreign word, compare Sanskrit pîta (properly yellow )); — named with other precious stones Ezek 28:13 ; Exod 28:17 = 39:10 ; construct מִּטְדַתכּֿוּשׁ Job 28:19 . — See Plin NH xxxvii. 8 -32 , Houghton in Sm DB, Topaz Ri HWB, Edelstein .
